name: Materials ordering, delivery notes and goods received on site
one_line: The organizational situation of PHYSICAL ARRIVAL: something was ordered for a site, a lorry brought some of it, somebody standing in mud signed for what actually came off the back, and the difference between the three is the whole point of the file. The organizing anchor is the DELIVERY EVENT at a site on a date, which is why it is a different situation from the order that preceded it and from the invoice that follows it - a delivery note is evidence of receipt, and the shortage scrawled on it is the reason anyone keeps it. Absorbs the legacy row cons.materials-delivery (ROW). Gist-level placeholder (J-IND): it recognizes the situation and writes NO field rows, because the construction_property schema declares none.

deterministic: PRECONDITION: every entry below is a DETECTION signal, never an extraction licence - this template's schema declares no field rows (PR-6; D1's deferral stands). “Privacy policy must be enforced before content reaches any model or external connector.”

a delivery-note structure: a delivery or advice note number, a DELIVER-TO address that differs from the invoice-to address, line items with quantities delivered - often against a separate ordered column - and a received-by signature block with a printed name and a time. The deliver-to versus invoice-to split is the discriminating shape and it exists in no other document in this family.

a goods-received or discrepancy annotation: a quantity struck through and rewritten, a shortage or damage note, or a 'received unchecked' endorsement across the signature. A document that carries a correction made at the point of handover is structurally unlike any other file here.
a proof-of-delivery capture: a photographed or scanned note, or a carrier-generated POD with a timestamp, a geolocation line and a signature image.
a purchase-order structure with a site delivery address and a requested delivery date - the ordering half of the same situation, distinguishable from a payment demand by its ORDER framing.

a waste transfer or duty-of-care note: the mirror movement off site, with a carrier registration, a waste description code and a transfer date. It is a delivery event running backwards and it files with the deliveries.

a materials schedule or take-off: quantities required by item, against which deliveries are booked in. “Tables matter because resumes, forms, applications, invoices, and administrative documents often place their most useful information in cells rather than body paragraphs.”

a product data or conformity attachment travelling with a load - a batch or heat number, a test certificate, a declaration of performance - which is kept because it evidences what was actually installed.
needs_llm: PRECONDITION: any model step runs after P7 and under the user's policy, and must abstain rather than guess: “A model that cannot cite sufficient evidence must return unknown.”

separating a delivery note from the supplier's invoice for the same load. They carry the same supplier, the same lines and often the same reference, and only one of them is a demand for payment. “Topic answers what a file is about, while purpose answers what the file was for.”
reading a handwritten shortage or damage annotation off a photographed note, where the printed lines OCR cleanly and the thing that matters does not.
deciding whether a photograph of a pallet on a pavement is delivery evidence, progress photography, or a damage claim - the same image serves all three and only context decides.
recognising a merchant's monthly statement as an accounting document rather than a delivery record, when it lists the same delivery-note numbers.
a delivery pack that is purpose-coherent and content-incoherent: a note, two certificates, a photograph and a signed sheet. “The documents are content-incoherent but purpose-coherent.”
never_alone: a supplier's or builders' merchant's name alone. It is on the delivery note, the invoice, the statement, the catalogue and the marketing email, and a folder of merchant-named PDFs is usually accounts payable - read across by inference from “A university name alone should not create a group because Columbia can appear as an authoring school, course provider, target institution, employer, research venue, or merely a cited organization.”
an address token alone: the deliver-to address, the invoice-to address and the letterhead address are three different things on one page.
a quantity or a unit token alone - orders, takeoffs, invoices, valuations and stock counts all carry them.
a signature image alone. A scrawl proves a handover happened, not what was in it.
a bare 4-digit number: a note number, an order number, a batch number and a postcode fragment all look like years.

membership in a download session that pulled a month of merchant paperwork at once - “A session should never be treated as proof of topic, and it should not carry the same confidence as a hash match or a directly extracted document fact.”

an extension or a source_type alone - “The engine should treat the file extension as a routing signal rather than an assumption about meaning, inspect the real MIME type or file signature where possible, and dispatch each file to a type-specific extractor.”

work_types: batch, test or conformity certificate travelling with a load
merchant statement (boundary case, usually not this row)
grouping_reasons: one delivery event: the note, the photograph taken of it, the discrepancy report and any certificates that came with the load - joined by a site, a date and a note number rather than by content.
one order across its part-deliveries, which is the reason the situation exists at all: a single order arrives in four loads over three weeks and only the set shows whether it all came.
one site's deliveries over the life of a job, which is a running record and the thing a shortage argument is reconstructed from.

a note and the invoice that quotes it - a real reason to join files, and the one most likely to tempt a delivery fact onto an unrelated invoice from the same merchant. “The graph does not automatically copy those missing facts onto sparse files.”
no group at all is a valid outcome: an isolated signed note for a one-off collection is a standalone record.

template.why: Empty by binding contract: construction_property declares no field rows (J-IND / PR-6, D1's deferral as narrowed, _CONTRACT rules 10 and 15), so no dimension can branch - a dimension naming an undeclared field opens a tree level no fact could ever fill. Held as prose for the pass that may license fields: the anchor is the SITE or job, then the order, then the delivery date. Supplier must sit below site rather than above it: a merchant-first tree scatters one job's deliveries across five merchants and hides the only question anyone asks of these files, which is whether everything ordered for this job actually arrived. “The recommendation should follow the practical rule that a parent dimension should provide the context required to understand the child.” - a delivery note is unintelligible without knowing which site it landed at. Not time-first at the top: “For document and record domains, project, function, or subject usually comes before time because putting year first scatters related work across calendar folders.” - though a delivery date is the natural leaf, because within one order the event IS the date. Privacy caveat specific to this row: delivery notes name the individuals who signed for goods and carry site addresses and, on carrier PODs, geolocation - none of which should become a destination dimension or reach a model prompt by default. The user may reverse, remove or flatten any of this later; this is a recommendation, not a frozen filesystem.

collides_with.signal: The sharpest collision: the delivery note and the supplier invoice for the same load carry the same merchant, the same lines and often the same reference. The discriminating evidence: a deliver-to address distinct from an invoice-to address, quantity columns, and a received-by signature supports this row; an invoice number, tax treatment, payment terms and a statement balance supports bookkeeping. A merchant name alone discriminates neither.

The ordering half overlaps that row's purchase-order half exactly, and both are authored to include POs. The discriminating evidence: a bounded competitive event with a solicitation reference, responses and an award supports the sourcing row; a routine site call-off against a materials schedule, and above all the ARRIVAL evidence, supports this row. Reciprocal to the open_question that row already carries about where POs belong.

Trade counter ordering and stock replenishment use the same order and delivery-note shapes at high volume. The discriminating evidence: replenishment against a catalogue and a stockroom supports the retail row; delivery to a named site for a specific job supports this row.

Carrier PODs, consignment notes and tracking exports are the same evidence class. The discriminating evidence: a consignment or waybill reference, a carrier's own network and a transport leg supports the logistics row; receipt of materials at a construction site supports this row.

Conformity declarations, batch certificates and waste transfer notes travel with loads and are also statutory records. The discriminating evidence: a regime, an inspection and a validity period supports the certificate row; arrival at a site on a date supports this row. This one is a genuine shared file rather than a mistake, and both rows should retrieve it.

A machine delivered to site arrives on a note that looks like a materials delivery. The discriminating evidence: an asset identity with an on-hire and off-hire period supports the plant row; consumed materials with quantities supports this row.

Shortage and damage records become the substantiation of a claim. The discriminating evidence: an assertion of entitlement with a narrative and a cost consequence supports the claim row; the contemporaneous record of what arrived supports this row.

A photograph of a pallet on site is delivery evidence in one folder and progress photography in another - the same bytes. The discriminating evidence: a photographed DOCUMENT, or an image whose accepted group is a delivery event, supports this row; an image of the state of the works supports the progress row. Stated reciprocally.

falls_through_to.why: The primary residual for this row, and it fits it better than any other in the family: an isolated delivery note or order confirmation with no accepted group is exactly this. “Receipts and Confirmations may hold isolated invoices, delivery confirmations, booking records, boarding passes, purchase receipts, event tickets, and similar transactional documents.”

The home for a standalone certificate, waste transfer note or order that has a durable purpose but no delivery group around it. “Independent Records may live under Personal/Independent Records and hold standalone certificates, notices, confirmations, forms, and PDFs that have a durable purpose but no broader group.”

The correct home for a lone photographed note or pallet with no accepted delivery group - it is an image with no event association, not a document. “One-Off Images may live under Photos/One-Off Images and hold images with no event, project, reference collection, or photo-family association.”

The cautious outcome for a scanned goods-received sheet whose numbers OCR badly, or a take-off whose job is unresolved. “Review Later may hold files whose meaning is partly understood but whose final location requires a future decision.”

The safe outcome for an unreadable carrier export or a damaged archive of photographed notes. “Unsupported or Encrypted may hold—or, more safely, represent without moving—password-protected archives, unreadable documents, damaged files, and unknown formats.”

sensitivity_why: Delivery paperwork is mundane and still carries three things that are not: the printed names and signatures of the individuals who received goods, the site address (which for domestic work is a private person's home), and, on carrier proofs of delivery and on phone photographs of notes, precise geolocation. 00 names the corpus this product handles - it “can include identity documents, account statements, tax records, medical information, legal records, credentials, private correspondence, GPS metadata, employment materials, and educational records.” - and GPS metadata is on that list by name. The operative limits are 00's: “Protected material should not be included in cloud-model prompts by default, should not display raw content in general group summaries, and should not be moved automatically without a user policy that explicitly permits it.” This row assigns only the catalogue value potentially_sensitive; it does not assign, alias, rank, or infer a P7 handling class.
open_question: Whether the ORDER belongs in this row at all. The roster hint says the paper trail between a purchase order and a site, and that is how a site keeps it - the order and the note are compared to each other or neither is worth keeping. But business_operations.procurement-sourcing was authored to hold purchase orders, and carries its own open question about whether POs belong to the event or to the money. Three rows therefore have a claim on one document type, and the honest answer is that a construction site's call-off against a materials schedule is a different animal from a competitively sourced purchase order even though both print the letters PO. Where that line falls is Joseph's. Recorded reciprocally so the question is visible from either side.
